question: Which organization publishes the annual 'World Happiness Report' that ranks countries based on their citizens' happiness levels?

options.text: United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)

solution:
The correct answer is __**United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Happiness Report** is an annual publication that ranks countries based on how happy their citizens perceive themselves to be. It is published by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**. **Hence, option 3 is correct.**
 
• The report was first released in **2012** to coincide with the **United Nations High-Level Meeting** on **Happiness and Well-being**. It has since become a global standard for measuring the quality of life and social progress.
 
• The rankings are primarily based on data from the **Gallup World Poll**, where respondents evaluate their own lives using the **Cantril Ladder** scale.
 
• The **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** is not the publisher of this report; it is well-known for publishing the **Human Development Report (HDR)** and the **Human Development Index (HDI)**. **Hence, option 1 is incorrect.**
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** focuses on international public health and publishes reports such as the **World Health Statistics**, but it does not produce the World Happiness Report. **Hence, option 2 is incorrect.**
 
• The **World Economic Forum (WEF)** is an international non-governmental organization that publishes the **Global Gender Gap Report** and the **Global Risk Report**, but it is not responsible for the happiness rankings. **Hence, option 4 is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Methodology of the Report:** The report uses six key variables to explain the variation in happiness levels across different nations: **GDP per capita**, **social support**, **healthy life expectancy**, **freedom to make life choices**, **generosity**, and **perceptions of corruption**.
 
• **Top Performing Countries:** Nordic countries consistently dominate the top of the rankings. **Finland** has been named the **happiest country in the world** for **seven consecutive years** as of the **2024** report. Other top-ranked nations include **Denmark**, **Iceland**, and **Sweden**.
 
• **India’s Ranking:** In the **2024 World Happiness Report**, **India** was ranked **126th** out of **143 countries**. This position remained unchanged from the previous year, indicating a need for improvement in social and economic well-being factors.
 
• **International Day of Happiness:** The report is typically released on or around **March 20**, which was designated as the **International Day of Happiness** by the **UN General Assembly** in **2012**.
 
• **The SDSN:** The **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** was established in **2012** under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General**. It works to mobilize global scientific and technological expertise to promote practical problem-solving for **sustainable development**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gross National Happiness (GNH):** The concept of measuring happiness as a metric of national progress was pioneered by **Bhutan**. In **1972**, the **Fourth King of Bhutan**, **Jigme Singye Wangchuck**, declared that **Gross National Happiness** is more important than **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.
 
• **Global Trends:** The **2024 report** noted a significant trend where **younger generations** in **North America** and parts of **Western Europe** reported lower happiness levels compared to older generations, a shift from historical patterns.
 
• **Policy Impact:** The findings of the **World Happiness Report** are increasingly used by governments to inform **public policy**. Countries like **New Zealand** and the **United Arab Emirates** have even appointed **Ministers of Happiness** or Well-being to integrate these metrics into governance.
 
• **Data Source:** The **Gallup World Poll** remains the primary data source, conducting surveys in more than **160 countries** and in over **140 languages** to capture a representative sample of the global population.
